questions.question_text: Which of the following is closest to the meaning of empathy as a psychiatric term?

options.text: Feeling sorry about the patient's problems
Feeling oneself into the patient's difficulties
Giving advice to patients about their problems

correct_answer.text: Feeling oneself into the patient's difficulties

correct_answers.text: Feeling oneself into the patient's difficulties

questions.explanation: Empathy is a skill used in an interview to assess the patient's internal subjective state by putting oneself into his /her shoes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a closed question?

options.text: At what time do you wake?

questions.explanation: It is important to allow the patient as far as possible to describe the problem spontaneously.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not advisable while interviewing a violent patient?

options.text: Getting close to the patient physically
Watching out for signs of increasing anger

correct_answer.text: Getting close to the patient physically

correct_answers.text: Getting close to the patient physically

questions.explanation: It is advisable not to approach the patient too closely and to avoid prolonged eye contact.

questions.question_text: Details of a patient's childhood relationship with his /her parents is part of:
questions.explanation: Any prolonged separation from parents and the patient's reaction to it, excessive fears, etc. should be assessed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes a patient who appears cheerful while describing sad events?
questions.explanation: Although the abnormality of incongruity of affect is said to be highly characteristic of schizophrenia, different interviewers tend to disagree about its presence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true about assessing risk of suicide?

options.text: It is an important part of mental state examination
It should be asked about in stages
It should be explored in detail
Is an important clinical skill to be learned
It carries the risk of suggesting suicide to people who are depressed

correct_answer.text: It carries the risk of suggesting suicide to people who are depressed

correct_answers.text: It carries the risk of suggesting suicide to people who are depressed

questions.explanation: Questioning about suicide during examination does not suggest suicide to people who have no suicidal inclination.

questions.question_text: A person who reports having heard his name called out while waking up from sleep is likely to have:
questions.explanation: Hypnapompic hallucinations occur when waking up from sleep. They are usually auditory but can be visual or tactile. They occur in normal people.

questions.question_text: Serial sevens is a test of: (see explanation)
questions.explanation:
Note:in the book it chooses "short term memory",
Serial sevens is included in the Mini Mental State Examination

questions.question_text: A patient reporting that people sitting at a distance are discussing him is likely to have:
questions.explanation: Extracampine hallucinations may also present in a similar way, when a patient experiences hallucinations outside the limits of the sensory field (concrete awareness).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an important task at the time of initial psychiatric interview?
questions.explanation: Establishing a diagnosis is not an important task in the initial psychiatric interview.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not fit into Bleuler's description of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: The primary symptoms of schizophrenia are known as the four 'A's: associative disturbances; affective disturbances; autism; and ambivalence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a disorder of perception?
questions.explanation: Abnormal perception includes sensory distortion and false perception.

questions.question_text: In a patient with spinal cord injury, which of the following does not indicate posterior column damage?
questions.explanation: Fine touch, pressure, vibration, position sensation, tactile discrimination, tactile localization and stereognosis are the posterior column sensations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of an upper motor neuron lesion?
questions.explanation: Cog-wheel rigidity is not a feature of upper motor neuron lesions. In peripheral nerves, these lesions occur above the level of the anterior horn cells in the spinal cord and in cranial nerves, they occur above the level of the motor nuclei.

questions.question_text: Which of the following illnesses can present with diplopia?
questions.explanation: The oculomotor nerve supplies the extraocular muscles except superior oblique and lateral rectus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of normal-pressure hydrocephalus?

options.text: Enlarged ventricles on CT brain scan

questions.explanation: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus is a treatable cause of cognitive impairment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions does not present with nystagmus?
questions.explanation: The frontal cortex is associated with functions like mood, personality and executive functions and language.

questions.question_text: A patient presenting with sensory and motor deficits in the right lower limb along with clouding of consciousness is likely to have developed:
questions.explanation: Unilateral occlusion of the anterior cerebral artery produces contralateral sensorimotor deficits mainly involving the lower extremity, but sparing the face and hands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is involved in the direct and consensual lights reflex pathway?
questions.explanation: Ciliary ganglion is a feature of Argyll Robertson pupil, which is seen in syphilis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is most likely to be damaged in a patient presenting with left homonymous hemianopia?
questions.explanation: Hemianopia is loss of half of the visual field.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a cerebellar sign?
questions.explanation: Intention tremor is seen.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions will not be part of the differential diagnosis in a patient presenting with papilloedema?
questions.explanation: Papilloedema is seen in increased intracranial pressure.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is likely to be seen in cerebral artery occlusion?
questions.explanation: Ipsilateral means same side.

questions.question_text: Colour vision is tested with the help of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Snellen chart tests visual acuity.

questions.question_text: 'Tunnel vision' is characteristic of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Retinitis pigmentosa is an inherited retinal degeneration.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not associated with Argyll Robertson pupil?

options.text: Lack of sympathetic nerve supply to the pupil

correct_answer.text: Lack of sympathetic nerve supply to the pupil

correct_answers.text: Lack of sympathetic nerve supply to the pupil

questions.explanation: The loss of sympathetic fibres occurs in Horner's syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ocular muscles is not supplied by the third cranial nerves?
questions.explanation: The oculomotor nerve supplies the extraocular muscles except superior oblique and lateral rectus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true of Bell's palsy?

options.text: It is lower motor neuron palsy of facial nerve
It causes difficulty in shutting eyes
It causes difficulty in raising eyebrows
It produces a loss of sense of taste

questions.explanation: Bell's palsy is usually unilateral.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about the trigeminal nerve?

options.text: It consists of motor and sensory components
Motor components supply the muscles of swallowing
Sensory components are responsible for general sensations to the face
It is responsible for the consensual component of corneal reflex
It is the motor supply to the muscles of mastication

correct_answer.text: Motor components supply the muscles of swallowing

correct_answers.text: Motor components supply the muscles of swallowing

questions.explanation: Trigeminal nerves supply the muscles of mastication and not of swallowing.

questions.question_text: While examining deep tendon reflexes, which of the following reflex and associated spinal segment pairs is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Knee jerk is supplied by L3 and 4.

questions.question_text: While examining gait disturbances, which of the following pairs of gait disturbance and common cause is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Marche a `petits pas is classically seen in hydrocephalus.

questions.question_text: Visual field defects affecting both eyes are indicative of a lesion at which of the following levels?

options.text: Lesions of or behind the optic chiasma

correct_answer.text: Lesions of or behind the optic chiasma

correct_answers.text: Lesions of or behind the optic chiasma

questions.explanation: Optic chiasma is the part of the brain where the optic nerves partially cross.

questions.question_text: On fundoscopy, a patient presents with unilateral papilloedema. Which of the following conditions could be the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Optic glioma is the most common primary neoplasm of the optic nerve.

questions.question_text: A Kayser–Fleischer ring is characteristic of which of the following?
questions.explanation: A Kayser–Fleischer ring reflects copper deposition in the brain.

questions.question_text: A positive Romberg's sign is indicative of which of the following?
questions.explanation: A positive Romberg test suggests sensory ataxia.

questions.question_text: In a patient presenting with a wrist drop, which of the following nerves is most likely to be affected?
questions.explanation: Radial neuropathy typically presents with weakness of wrist dorsiflexion (i.e. wrist drop) and finger extension.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a test of attention and concentration?

options.text: Timed letter or star cancellation task

questions.explanation: Cognitive estimates is a test of frontal lobe functions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a definition of semantic memory?

options.text: Memory of words and their meanings
Memory of facts and concepts and words and their meanings

correct_answer.text: Memory of facts and concepts and words and their meanings

correct_answers.text: Memory of facts and concepts and words and their meanings

questions.explanation: Semantic dementia is one of the main clinical variants (progressive aphasia) of frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: Episodic and semantic memory are components of which of the following memory systems?
questions.explanation: There are two types of long-term memory: episodic memory and semantic memory.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive functions is not attributed to frontal lobes?
questions.explanation: Praxis is attributed to parietal lobes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is less likely to present with a disorder of frontal lobes?
questions.explanation: In Pick's disease, knife-blade atrophy is seen.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tests is not used for frontal lobe function?
questions.explanation: Digit span tests attention and concentration.

questions.question_text: While differentiating between delirium and dementia, which of the following cognitive domains is less likely to be affected in dementia?
questions.explanation: Attention and awareness are usually unaffected in dementia and delirious patients have fluctuating attention.

questions.question_text: Which of the following dementias can present with a classical mixture of cortical and sub-cortical features?
questions.explanation: Lewy body dementia presents with memory problems and Parkinsonian symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive functions is not localized in the non-dominant hemisphere?
questions.explanation: Praxis is localized mainly in the dominant parietal lobe.

questions.question_text: Which of the following areas in the brain is responsible for language comprehension and production?
questions.explanation: Broca's area is located in the left posterior inferior front cortex comprising Brodmann's areas 44 and 45. Wernicke's area is on the posterior section of the superior temporal gyrus posterior part of Brodmann's area 22.

questions.question_text: Which of the following terms refers to the correct use of prepositions, pronouns, adverbs and verbs in a language?
questions.explanation: Syntax means the assembly of strings of words into sentences using pronouns, prepositions, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a definition of dyslexia?
questions.explanation: Apraxia is the inability to carry out learned purposeful movements.

questions.question_text: A tendency to produce erroneous material to fill in the gaps on being questioned about past events is known as:
questions.explanation: Confabulation is seen in Korsakoff's psychosis.

questions.question_text: A patient has presented with left-sided neglect. Which of the following areas of the brain is most likely to be affected?
questions.explanation: The right parietal and prefrontal cortex is involved in spatial attention.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not apply to dressing apraxia?

options.text: It is a disorder of the motor coordination of the upper limbs
It is a disorder of visual–spatial mechanisms
It may be seen in advanced dementia
It may be seen in focal lesions of the right parietal cortex

questions.explanation: Dressing apraxia is not a motor disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Kluver–Bucy syndrome?
questions.explanation: The amygdala and hypothalamus are involved in Kluver–Bucy syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a dominant (left) hemisphere function?
questions.explanation: Construction is a non-dominant (right) hemisphere function.

questions.question_text: In a patient in the early stage of Alzheimer's disease, which of the following tests can be used to estimate pre-morbid IQ?
questions.explanation: The National Adult Reading Test (NART) is widely used as a measure of premorbid IQ of English-speaking patients with dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about most tests of intellectual ability?

options.text: Almost all are completely free from practice effect
They are not affected by language

questions.explanation: In most tests of intellectual ability, the subject's educational level can have a major effect on performance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true about the Wisconsin Card-Sorting Test?

options.text: It is used to study abstract behaviour
It is used to study set-shifting ability
People with frontal lobe damage score low
People with subcortical dementia score normal

correct_answer.text: People with subcortical dementia score normal

correct_answers.text: People with subcortical dementia score normal

questions.explanation: Subjects with subcortical dementia fail on this test.

questions.question_text: Which of the following calculation difficulties is most likely to be seen in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease?
questions.explanation: Acalculia is associated with parietal lobe dysfunction.
